claim_summary: TimeSage-EV provides a live, cutoff-isolated benchmark for recurring time-series analysis and introduces a diagnostic skill library that agents can induce and reuse across periods.

claim_evidence.quote: We introduce TimeSage-EV, a live benchmark for agentic time series analysis in evolving environments.
Experiments with frontier LLM agents and TimeSage-1.0, a novel self-evolving agent with a reusable analytical skill library

modules.name: Live cutoff-isolated time-series benchmark
modules.scope_reason: R3_1 TSK is no: this benchmark evaluates multiple kinds of recurring analysis, and changing task family does not require redesigning its temporal cutoff environment. R3_2 GTS is yes because its evidence states and cutoffs depend on release chronology; GH would apply only if the mechanism managed execution without temporal semantics.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - benchmark covers multiple analytical outputs; cutoff logic is not bound to one task objective
R3_2_GTS:yes - evidence and cutoff are period-specific

evidence.quote: We construct TimeSage-EV, a live benchmark
The agent receives pre-cutoff time series data and documents, while the target-period release is withheld for verification.

modules.name: Reusable Python skill induction, quality check and retrieval
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:no: induct_skill/retrieve_skill and the quality check do not encode a task output or verifier. R3_2_GTS:no: saving, checking (callable, self-contained, faithful description, not a literal answer) and retrieving Python routines does not use time order, windows, frequency or information availability. R3_3_GH:yes: tool and state management.
rubric_path: R3_2_GTS:no - induction, quality check, retrieval carry no temporal semantics
R4:Memory and Context; Tools and Execution; Optimization and Evolution

evidence.quote: It adds two tools: induct_skill saves a small reusable Python function with a name, description, and notes when the agent identifies a recurring analysis idiom, and retrieve_skill returns the full body of a saved skill when its short description is insufficient for reliable use.
Before a skill is exposed in later periods, a check enforces that it is a callable, self-contained routine with a usable interface and a faithful description

modules.name: Next-period skill activation
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK:no: the activation rule is independent of any task output. R3_2_GTS:yes: an accepted skill becomes available only from the next period, an information-availability rule that keeps later answers from using same-period induction.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - not bound to a task objective
R3_2_GTS:yes - availability tied to period chronology
R4:Memory and Context; Optimization and Evolution

evidence.quote: Accepted skills become callable tools from the next period, so a skill induced in the period tk cannot alter the current answer but can affect behavior in tk+1 and beyond.

temporal_validity.quote: whether the report’s claims are supported by cutoffvalid evidence rather than future or unsupported information

reconciliation.reason: Keep the same benchmark mechanism and id. The packet describes a live environment with cumulative series, prior documents, and withheld target releases; this supports a GTS resource-level evaluation module with data-management and temporal-validation functions.

notes: The benchmark is the work's primary contribution, with TimeSage-1.0 included as a diagnostic method. The skill library and next-period registration are parts of one temporal reuse mechanism.

items.reason: The tools induct_skill and retrieve_skill and the quality check (callable, self-contained routine, faithful description) use no temporal order, windows or availability; R3_3 applies.

items.result: split back out as a GTS module
items.reason: Accepted skills become callable only from the next period; this availability rule can be reused separately from the library and is the part that carries temporal semantics (R3_2).

adjudication.summary: The skill library itself is a general runtime module (GH); the next-period activation rule is a separate GTS module. The benchmark module is accepted unchanged.
